findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the completion sidecar criteria[] persistence (completion_sidecar.py) and the completion_verdict.schema.json criteria[].met field as consumers, and state how the tri-state per-criterion value survives (or is deliberately projected) through them.
evidence: completion_sidecar.py:335 persists 'criteria': v.get('criteria', []) — the lossless per-criterion capture
completion_verdict.schema.json:31: criteria[].met is 'type':'boolean'
Scope names only assemble_deterministic_verdict and merge_finalizer_with_bank as the criteria[]-emitting seams, not the sidecar/schema that persist their output
findings.finding: A tri-state per-criterion value threads into the persisted verdict's criteria[] records, but the completion sidecar PASS-capture (src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py) and the completion_verdict.schema.json criteria[].met field (typed boolean) are unenumerated consumers that would coerce or drop the new state on the lossless PASS record.
scenarios: A PASS-with-insufficient-evidence-criterion (or the backfilled criteria[] record) reaches the sidecar; the boolean-typed schema field coerces/rejects the tri-state, losing the distinction the plan's ACs require to survive

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how `insufficient_evidence` is represented in the completion_verdict schema (per-criterion `met` is strictly boolean and verdict is PASS/FAIL-only) so the tri-state survives to the signed verdict rather than being rejected or silently coerced.
evidence: schema line 31: per-criterion `met` is `{"type": "boolean"}` — a null or sentinel value is invalid/dropped
schema line 11-12: top-level `verdict` normalizes to PASS/FAIL, no third token
both rendering seams' output is validated against output_schema="completion_verdict" (completion_recovery.py:674, :774)
plan's suggested widening 'met: bool | None plus an explicit state field' produces a value the schema cannot carry
the Scope/Acceptance sections never mention completion_verdict.schema.json
findings.finding: The tri-state banking mechanism collides with the completion_verdict schema, which types per-criterion `met` as strict boolean and normalizes verdict to PASS/FAIL only; the plan never addresses schema representability of `insufficient_evidence`.
findings.location: Proposed fix (CriterionBank.upsert widening + both rendering seams); src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json:10-12,31
scenarios: a merged or deterministic verdict carrying an insufficient_evidence criterion is validated against the schema and either rejected or has the tri-state distinction silently discarded

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `_validate_coverage` (completion_recovery.py:364,:370) to the scope: its `isinstance(met, bool)` gate and its PASS/unmet check must tolerate the insufficient_evidence value instead of raising 'untyped criterion decision'.
evidence: completion_recovery.py:364: `if any(not isinstance(record.get("met"), bool) for record in records): raise CompletionRecoveryError('...returned an untyped criterion decision')`
:717 runs `_validate_coverage(merged, ...)` on the output of merge_finalizer_with_bank — the exact seam the plan widens
:370 `if verdict == 'PASS' and any(not record['met'] ...)` also assumes bool met
findings.finding: The plan enumerates chokepoints but misses `_validate_coverage`, which hard-raises CompletionRecoveryError on any non-bool `met` and runs on the merged verdict — an insufficient_evidence sentinel will fail-loud there.
scenarios: merge_finalizer_with_bank backfills an insufficient_evidence entry; _validate_coverage raises 'untyped criterion decision' and the finalizer attempt is discarded, falling through to deterministic fallback or a hard recovery error

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Include `_run_finalizer` (completion_recovery.py:741) in scope: the banked_evidence handed to the LLM finalizer coerces met to bool and must convey insufficient_evidence instead of collapsing it to false.
evidence: completion_recovery.py:741: `"met": bool(entry.get("met")),` inside banked_evidence built for the finalizer prompt
plan asserts 'there are TWO verdict-rendering seams, both of which currently coerce the banked value to a bool'
findings.finding: The plan claims exactly TWO rendering seams coerce banked met to bool, but `_run_finalizer` is a third that coerces `bool(entry.get('met'))` when feeding banked evidence to the LLM finalizer, collapsing insufficient_evidence to false before the model sees it.
scenarios: the LLM finalizer is handed banked_evidence where an exhausted criterion appears as met=false, so the model reasons over a false negative and may emit a FAIL — the same misattribution the fix targets, reintroduced upstream of the two named seams

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the never-banked/exhausted placeholder branch (met=false+exhausted=True, completion_banking.py:641-661 and the parallel merge branch) also renders indeterminate-with-remediation, or explicitly justify why only the banked branch changes.
evidence: completion_banking.py:646-660: unbanked criteria set met:False, exhausted:True, and a 'recovery budget exhausted' high-severity FAIL finding
Plan scopes only the entry-is-None-false branch: 'assemble_deterministic_verdict (completion_banking.py:619-640, met = bool(entry.get(...)) + FAIL finding)'
T8: an unspecified fallback for an incomplete/failed sub-step — the never-banked (also exhausted) criterion is absence-of-evidence rendered as FAIL, the very defect being fixed, left untouched
findings.finding: assemble_deterministic_verdict (and merge_finalizer_with_bank) has a SECOND absence-of-evidence seam — the unbanked/exhausted placeholder branch that also emits met=false + a high-severity FAIL finding — which the plan does not bring into the tri-state treatment.
scenarios: A criterion the recovery loop never reached at all (no bank entry) still renders FAIL 'not met' rather than indeterminate, so the honesty fix only covers criteria that reached the exhaustion banking site

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive the banked-`met` consumer inventory via find_referencing_symbols on CriterionBank.upsert plus a grep sweep for get("met")/record["met"], and extend Scope to cover the tri-state at _run_finalizer (completion_recovery.py:741), _validate_coverage (:364), audit/page.py:318, and the truthiness verdict/findings logic inside merge_finalizer_with_bank (completion_banking.py:725, :760) — not only the bool() coercion at :710.
evidence: Plan: "there are TWO verdict-rendering seams, both of which currently coerce the banked value to a bool: assemble_deterministic_verdict (completion_banking.py:619-640 ...) and merge_finalizer_with_bank (completion_banking.py:705-714 ...)"

completion_recovery.py:741: `"met": bool(entry.get("met")),` inside _run_finalizer builds the banked_evidence payload handed to the LLM finalizer — a tri-state entry is flattened to False before the finalizer runs (not in Scope)
completion_recovery.py:364: `if any(not isinstance(record.get("met"), bool) for record in records):` raises CompletionRecoveryError on a non-bool met (not in Scope)
audit/page.py:318: `met = bool(c.get("met"))` renders the PASS criteria table (not in Scope)

completion_banking.py:725 `any_unmet = any(not r["met"] for r in records)` and :760 `if record["met"]: continue` — within merge_finalizer_with_bank, verdict class and findings use truthiness, so met=='insufficient_evidence' (truthy) is treated as MET, contradicting the plan's fail-closed requirement; the plan's cited :710 bool() coercion is not the site that decides the verdict
findings.finding: The plan asserts 'there are TWO verdict-rendering seams' and scopes exactly assemble_deterministic_verdict and merge_finalizer_with_bank, but the banked `met` value is consumed at additional sites the inventory omits. A grep of `get("met")` / `record["met"]` surfaces: completion_recovery.py:741 (_run_finalizer flattens `met: bool(entry.get('met'))` into the finalizer payload), completion_recovery.py:364 (_validate_coverage rejects non-bool `met`), and audit/page.py:318 (_completion_section renders `bool(c.get('met'))`). Additionally, inside the named merge_finalizer_with_bank the verdict/findings decisions use truthiness (`not r['met']` at :725, `if record['met']` at :760 in _findings_for_unmet), not the `bool()` coercion the plan cites at :710 — so a truthy 'insufficient_evidence' string would be classed MET, not blocked.
findings.location: Scope / "there are TWO verdict-rendering seams, both of which currently coerce the banked value to a bool: assemble_deterministic_verdict ... and merge_finalizer_with_bank"
scenarios: completion_recovery.py:741 (_run_finalizer): a banked insufficient_evidence entry is coerced to met=False in the finalizer payload, so the LLM finalizer sees a hard negative — reintroducing the absence-of-evidence-as-evidence-of-absence confusion the fix targets, on the primary (LLM finalizer) path rather than the fallback path

completion_banking.py:725/760 (inside the named merge_finalizer_with_bank): met=='insufficient_evidence' is truthy, so `not r['met']` is False and `if record['met']` is True — the criterion is classed MET and generates no unmet finding, so the close gate does NOT block, directly defeating the plan's stated fail-closed requirement
audit/page.py:318 (_completion_section): an insufficient_evidence criterion renders as a met=false row in the audit PASS table with no indeterminate distinction
completion_recovery.py:364 (_validate_coverage): if a tri-state met reaches a finalizer output record, coverage validation raises CompletionRecoveryError
findings.suggested_fix: Add these sites to Scope: (1) _run_finalizer must forward the tri-state (or an explicit indeterminate marker) to the finalizer rather than bool()-flattening it; (2) merge_finalizer_with_bank's :725 any_unmet and _findings_for_unmet :760 must treat insufficient_evidence as blocking/indeterminate, not as truthy-MET; (3) _validate_coverage must admit the tri-state; (4) audit/page.py _completion_section must render insufficient_evidence distinctly from met=false.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Evaluate a per-criterion parallel marker (mirroring the existing `verdict_obtainable` pattern that rides alongside PASS/FAIL) versus widening the strictly-boolean `met`, and justify the chosen approach on schema/blast-radius grounds.
evidence: schema lines 14-18 (verdict_obtainable): 'OPTIONAL framework-set marker (never model-supplied)... a VERIFIER FAULT, not a judgement that a criterion is unmet... rides ALONGSIDE the PASS/FAIL vocabulary rather than adding a third verdict token, so verdict stays FAIL and every existing consumer still blocks fail-closed'
the plan reaches for the same 'absence-of-evidence, not evidence-of-absence, still fail-closed' semantics but proposes widening the boolean met rather than adding a parallel marker
findings.finding: The plan widens the strictly-boolean per-criterion `met` to a tri-state, but the codebase already carries a directly-applicable precedent — verdict_obtainable — a framework-set marker that rides ALONGSIDE PASS/FAIL without adding a third token; the plan does not consider this structurally-simpler alternative.
scenarios: a per-criterion insufficient_evidence marker riding alongside a boolean met would satisfy the schema unchanged, avoid the _validate_coverage bool gate, and reuse the fail-closed-but-honest pattern the codebase already establishes
